ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback! We apologize for your concerns with your new Spirit, that is not the experience we want our loyal Weber fans to have. We would like to help put your mind at ease.

Your grill should be able to reach the same high temperature we expect from all of our grills, at least 450 F. If your grill is not getting that hot, we would suggest starting by double-checking your current gas pressure. The gas pressure provided to the grill is of the utmost importance, it affects the performance of the burner tube(s).

There are a few things we would like to check. Let's start with the easy stuff:

1.) Please make sure that you consider "High" on your control knobs to be the 
first spot to your left (the 9:00 position). The further you go to the right,
the lower the temperature will be and all the way to the right is low.

2.) Please make sure you're always cooking with the lid down except when 
flipping the food halfway. The second you open the lid the heat escapes, 
and you'll need to close it to let the temperature recover.

3.) It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." 
What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it 
reduces the pressure. Follow the instructions to reset the bypass safety 
mode. 

Here is a helpful link for review:
https://www.weber.com/US/en/blog/burning-questions/why-wont-my-natural-gas-grill-get-hot/weber-29496.html

We would like to hear more about this experience. Please lookout for an email from our Support team.

Thank you for your feedback! We are sorry to hear your disappointment but yet understand your concerns about preheating your Spirit grill.

Allowing any grill to preheat for 10-15 minutes before using it, could possibly not allow your grill to reach the ideal cooking temperature when you put your food on it. Preheating also helps to eliminate hot spots and helps ensure your food cooks consistently & evenly. 

Not allowing your grill to properly preheat, may lead to problems with food sticking to the grates.
